extracted.intended_audience: developers and operators (DevOps/SRE/platform engineers) who install, configure, and operate HashiCorp Consul for service networking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for installing, configuring, and operating HashiCorp Consul to provide service discovery, service mesh, identity-based authorization, traffic management, observability, multi-tenancy, and automation across on‑prem and cloud environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage secure network connectivity across environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Consul is a service networking solution that enables teams to manage secure network connectivity between services, across on‑prem, hybrid cloud, and multi‑cloud environments and runtimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Consul features (service discovery, service mesh, identity, L7 traffic management, and service‑to‑service encryption) to ensure secure connectivity across diverse deployment environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service discovery and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Register your services to Consul: Deploy Consul client agents on your virtual machine workloads. Register services to Consul and set up health checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy Consul client agents on each workload/node, provide service definitions so agents can register services into the Consul catalog, and configure health checks so registered services are discoverable and their health is tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service mesh deployment and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Securely connect your services with Consul service mesh: Deploy Consul service mesh and secure your applications using Envoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy sidecar proxies (e.g., Envoy) or gateways as part of the data plane to enforce security, manage traffic, and enable service‑to‑service encryption and observability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity-based authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: In a datacenter, Consul uses identity to associate agents, configurations, and services on different nodes that may have different names but are otherwise identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Consul identity features to bind permissions and intentions to service or node identities rather than relying solely on names or addresses; this enables consistent authorization across environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-to-service encryption (mTLS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure service-to-service encryption: Consul provides secure service-to-service encryption; include new services in Consul service mesh gradually using permissive mTLS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable mTLS for encryption and consider permissive mTLS during migration to avoid breaking traffic while adding services to the mesh incrementally.

rubrics_metrics.name: L7 traffic management and advanced routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Control service traffic patterns with canary deployments, service splitters, chaos engineering practices, and Consul API Gateway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Consul traffic control features (service splitters, canaries) and the API Gateway for L7 routing and traffic shaping to implement progressive delivery and fault injection experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose mesh services externally via API Gateway
rubrics_metrics.description: Access services in your service mesh: Use Consul API Gateway to enable external access to services inside the mesh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When external access is needed, configure the Consul API Gateway to provide ingress to mesh services while preserving security and routing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observability for performance and debugging
rubrics_metrics.description: Consul observability features enhance your service mesh capabilities with enriched metrics, logs, and distributed traces so you can improve performance and debug your distributed services with precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument services and proxies to emit metrics, logs, and traces; integrate Consul observability outputs with your monitoring/tracing stack to detect and troubleshoot issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network automation based on catalog changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Automate infrastructure changes based on changes to the Consul catalog using Consul‑Terraform‑Sync and learn how Consul's built‑in load balancing features help applications automatically adapt to changes in services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Consul‑Terraform‑Sync (CTS) and Consul's load balancing primitives to drive automated infrastructure changes (e.g., updating routing/load balancers) in response to service registration or topology changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement multi‑tenancy with partitions, namespaces, and peering
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement multi-tenancy: Manage service tenancy with admin partitions, namespace, and cluster peering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use administrative partitions and namespaces to separate tenants and use cluster peering to connect multiple Consul clusters while maintaining isolation and appropriate access controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configuration entries govern security, traffic, and cluster behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Configuration entries explicitly define many of Consul's security, traffic, and cluster management behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author configuration entries to declare intentions, proxies, service defaults, and other policies that control security, traffic routing, and cluster management; treat configuration entries as the primary policy surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consul agent deployment and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consul agent is a long running daemon that operates on a node. It is a core unit of Consul operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run a Consul agent on every node participating in service discovery or mesh; understand whether the agent is operating as a client or server and configure accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data plane architecture: gateways and sidecar proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Consul can deploy gateways and sidecar proxies in an application's data plane to help you secure, observe, and manage application traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the data plane using sidecars for per‑service controls and gateways for ingress/egress and connectivity across networks or clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consul catalog correctness and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consul catalog API tracks registered services and their locations for both service discovery and service mesh use cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the catalog accurate and up to date by ensuring services register/unregister correctly and health checks reflect true service health; rely on the catalog for discovery and routing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster consensus and quorum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consul ensures a consistent state using the Raft protocol. A quorum, or a majority of server agents with one leader, agree to state changes before committing to the state log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate an appropriate number of server agents to achieve quorum and tolerate failures; design for leader election and safe state changes to avoid split‑brain or data loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership management via gossip (Serf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consul agents manage membership in datacenters and WAN federations using the Serf protocol, also called gossip communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure network connectivity and configuration (e.g., ports, ACLs) that allow Serf/gossip to function reliably for membership and failure detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consul editions and runtime tooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Consul releases include Enterprise and Community editions. Additional tool binaries for managing Consul on specific runtimes and cloud providers is also available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate Consul edition (Community vs Enterprise) and corresponding tool binaries for your runtime/cloud; be aware of feature differences between editions when planning deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Consul Terraform provider for IaC configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use the official Terraform provider to configure your Consul cluster's ACLs, configuration entries, intentions, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage Consul ACLs, intentions, configuration entries, and other resources using the Terraform provider to enforce reproducible, versioned infrastructure and policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation and developer mode options
rubrics_metrics.description: How to install Consul: Install Consul to get started with service discovery and service mesh. Follow the installation instructions to download the precompiled binary, or use Go to compile from source. Run Consul in developer mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow official install instructions for your environment (precompiled binaries or building from source). Use developer mode for local experimentation and learning, not production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification preparation (Consul Associate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare for the Consul Associate (003) certification exam: Choose to follow an in‑depth guide or to review select exam topics depending on the kind of preparation support you need. Then review sample questions to learn what to expect on exam day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the listed topics and sample questions if pursuing the Consul Associate certification to validate knowledge of Consul concepts and operations.
